quest.title: Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands
quest.description: Cyrus's strange situation puts everyone on alert, and Cyno went after him alone. As his friends, you, Paimon, and Tighnari could never turn a blind eye to his predicament.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we've made it to Caravan Ribat. Where should we go next?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe we should ask the nearby guards if they've seen anything?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hold on. Look over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that... Dehya?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You sure you wanna brave the desert alone? I mean, it's your choice at the end of the day, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's not my first time. I'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Cyno...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If you're really going through with this, then at least take our advice: When you're packing for your trip, budget for five days more than you plan to spend out there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Makes sense. Okay, I'll go get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Thought we might find you here. You're trying to retrace Cyrus's steps, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Didn't I tell you not to come after me? ...I thought I had a good lead on you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well sorry, but we never agreed to that. Why would you go off on your own like this?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Nothing personal. It's just a complex situation, and I'd rather not involve anyone else if I can help it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hah, takes a special kind of person to get Cyno chasing them all the way to Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But why so coy today, huh? You only gave us his age and description, why can't you reveal his name? ...Is he Sumeru's Most Wanted, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, also — hey guys! It's been a while!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya and Candace! So nice to see you! Actually, seeing all of our friends is the whole reason we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You're looking well. Glad to see it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Candace and I came to Caravan Ribat on business. We ran into Cyno as he was asking about some elderly gentleman's whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Some people here say they saw him. Guess he stood out as an older guy heading into the desert alone, with just a sumpter beast in tow, and very few supplies...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's gotta be one heck of a story there.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Cyno, it's okay if you can't tell us anything about the case. But let us know how we can support you.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: We're here to help however you need. The more people we have working on this, the quicker we'll be able to find the person you seek.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...No, it's not that simple. If I'm right, he'll be doing everything he can to avoid us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We spoke with Zaha Hadi. From what she said, it's pretty clear that he wants to try and solve this on his own. It won't be easy trying to find him in the desert when he's deliberately trying to cover his tracks.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Sounds like this is far more complex than we imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Still, if he started from Caravan Ribat, the chances are that his route took him via Aaru Village. You may as well ask if anyone there has seen him.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: My thanks to you both. Once this is resolved, I will find a way to repay you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah c'mon, no need to get all serious. Just buy a round of drinks next time we're all in the city, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's a deal.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alright. So... you all set?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes, we'll handle it from here. Thank you again for your help — I don't take it for granted.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alright, then we'll leave you to it. Just remember, if you change your mind and need some reinforcements, we'll be here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: And don't think you'd be imposing. You can depend on us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll keep him outta trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hold on... There's a few things I'd like to clear up.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Go on.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So, after you left the campsite, we had a longer talk...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. Clearly, we've only scratched the surface of the Temple of Silence question. It doesn't surprise me at all that the one in the Akademiya is a fake.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Do you have any connection with the Temple of Silence?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I do. I trust you're all aware of the spirit that gives me my power? Hermanubis, the original founder of the Temple of Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Due to my unique constitution, I was put through a number of trials in the desert when I was younger. Later, I met the professor, and he brought me to Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But my memory of that time is hazy. I can't recall much.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's a good thing that Kaveh noticed the emblem on the letter. Without that, I don't know if we would have connected the dots, and realized there was more to this case than mere extortion.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I did not recognize that symbol at all. Whether that's because I've never seen it, or because my memory fails me... it's hard to say.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right. Thank goodness for Kaveh, and for Alhaitham's diligence during his time as Acting Grand Sage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Cyrus must have recognized it right away, right? Otherwise, he wouldn't have had any qualms about you reporting it. Maybe his connection to the Temple of Silence goes even deeper than yours!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I suspect so too. Professor has never once mentioned the Temple of Silence in conversation. And whenever the conversation turns to Hermanubis and the concept of spirit indwelling, he avoids going into any depth.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, speaking of avoiding things — you do realize, don't you, now that we've caught up with you, you're stuck with us for the rest of the way?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I am aware. And I have accepted it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Or rather, I don't see how I could manage to ditch you en route. So I might as well accept that you're coming with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Fact is, we're coming with you whether you like it or not. So the best option now is to try to look out for each other. Ha!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can't get rid of us!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Then at least let me buy you a drink once we're back in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Works for me. Alright, off we go. Let's start by seeing what the guards here can tell us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Mahamatra Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm looking for someone, so I'd like to confirm any recent foot traffic in and out of Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno describes Cyrus's appearance and provisions.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: A man matching that description passed by Aaru Village not too long ago. He stopped by to load up on food and water, and feed his sumpter beast, then he was on his way.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Where was he going?

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Let me think... He took a seat by the entrance of the village for a while, and had a brief chat with the person who came to deliver the water. He said he was headed... somewhere near an oasis. But he didn't mention which one.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Do you have a map? I can mark out the direction he was heading and the best routes to any nearby oases.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I have one. Mark away.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Great.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: ...There you go.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Thank you so much. You were a great help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got a really good memory!

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Ah, you're quite welcome. Just doing my job.

dialogues.speaker: Fodil
dialogues.text: Best of luck. I hope you find him soon!

talks.objective: Head to the oasis and continue searching for clues

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hold on. I see some people over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think it's safe to ask them what they know?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Should be. I'll g—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No. I'll do it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why can't Cyno go talk to them? What difference does it make?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Given my background, appearance, and the way I dress, I might not be the most welcome visitor here. Just in case, it's probably better to let a more neutral party handle things.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hello there. Hope I'm not interrupting. My friend and I are looking for an elderly man who's gone missing around these parts. Any chance I could ask you a couple of questions?
Oh, a missing person, huh? Sure, sure, sure, what do you wanna know?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm just wondering if you've seen him. Let me give you the details...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tighnari describes Cyrus' appearance and clothing.
...So, a silver-haired guy in a long robe, cultured type with thoughtful eyes... And he's traveling alone.

dialogues.speaker: Carefree Desert-Dweller
dialogues.text: He'd stand out like a sore thumb around here.
Yeah. Sounds like the kind of guy we'd remember if we saw him.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (He's looking behind me?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh, that guy's looking our way...
Your friend over there stands out a lot, too.
Hey! Aren't you Cyno, the General Mahamatra?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me.
You don't seem surprised that I recognized you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It wouldn't be the first time.
You're the one looking for the old man who's gone missing, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (I have a bad feeling about this guy...)
Someone's on edge. You don't trust me much, do you?
No need to hide it, I understand why you're wary of us. Still, you came to us asking for help — do you want it or not?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I thought you were a group of merchants. Seems I was mistaken.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Your henchmen don't look like much. But something tells me they'd put up a better fight than most mercenaries.
Hey! Hear that, guys? You're my henchmen now.

dialogues.speaker: Carefree Desert-Dweller
dialogues.text: Suits me. As long as I get paid for it.

dialogues.speaker: Irritable Desert-Dweller
dialogues.text: Just cut to the chase already. I'm running out of patience.
Alright, alright, alright.
...Come with me, all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where are you taking us?
Don't you want to find your friend?
Silver-haired, long robe, cultured type with thoughtful eyes... Hahaha, sounds like there's a whole other side to Cyrus I didn't know about.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So you know where he is?
Just follow me. I'll take you to him.
In here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Where are you looking? There's nothing here...
Please step back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Something's coming out of the ground!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...What is this enormous building doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And how was it so well hidden? ...King Deshret's technology?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, so... Hold on, who are you guys, really...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is this... the Temple of Silence? So you're a member?
All good questions. There'll be plenty of time to address them later.
Alright. You can wait here for now.
I'll inform our leader that you've arrived at the Temple of Silence. Sit tight until he comes to greet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, so he's just gonna leave us here unattended? Maybe we're not being kidnapped after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: They can't have been at the oasis by chance. They were waiting for us... Whoever the leader is here, they were obviously counting on us showing up.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So this is the Temple of Silence?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: After leaving the rainforest... They hid themselves here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look. That guy's coming back.
Don't worry. Someone will come and call for you soon.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please. At least tell us what to call you.
Ah. Sorry, guess I was so delighted to see you, I forgot to introduce myself.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: My name is Sethos. I'll be here if you need me, but I'm not planning on answering all of your questions. Other than that, you can occupy yourselves however you see fit.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So we're free to explore by ourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Yep. I mean, I'm not worried about you running off.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Cyrus is here, and unless I've misunderstood — you're all quite anxious to see him again.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...He's right. Well, if we've got some time, we might as well take a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is not what Paimon was expecting to find in the desert... Especially not hidden right next to an oasis...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Paimon's scared...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They must have kidnapped Cyrus. D—Do you think this is the guy Urraca met in the tavern?
What's wrong? Thinking about your professor?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I just hope for your sake you haven't done anything you might regret.
Me too. I hope I haven't done anything to incur your wrath.

talks.objective: Wait for a bit, and talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I never imagined that the true Temple of Silence would be hidden somewhere like this... We've passed through these parts before, but never noticed anything.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's King Deshret's technology for you, I guess. It borders on the miraculous. Amazing to think that's it's been preserved intact all this time...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We should be wary of our hosts. Still, at this point we can be confident that the professor is safe and sound. So that's something.

talks.objective: Wait for a bit, and talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Sethos, have you got some time to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Although I'm assuming by "chat," you mean you have questions for me? Hahaha, I don't blame you. Anyone else would.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you get a lot of people asking you questions?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Not often. The Temple of Silence is a place of quiet and solitude. We don't get too many visitors.

choices.text: You were the one who tricked Urraca, right?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Yes, that was me. Although, "tricked" is a stretch. He was asking everyone in the tavern about ways to make some easy money.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: He insisted that nothing was off the table, even if it broke the law. So I told him that Cyrus had embezzled a large sum of Mora from the desert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you framed Cyrus for a crime that he did not commit!

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: No no no, that's not entirely true. Let me jog your memory — the letter just said that he had uncovered Cyrus's secret. It didn't say what secret that was.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you tell him to use that wording?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Of course. Urraca was a great accomplice, really. Very cooperative with a little bit of wine in him — did exactly what he was told... And not much of an original thinker though. It doesn't surprise me that he struggles academically.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why did Cyrus leave for the desert as soon as he received the letter?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: You'll have to ask him that one yourself. Certain things I can't answer for him. I'm neither judging nor defending him.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: All you need to know is that he recognized our emblem, and it was his own choice to take the bait.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Ahaha, what kind of a question is that? He's the General Mahamatra, everyone in Sumeru knows who he is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, but back at the oasis, you can't have known who he was for sure, or you wouldn't have asked him. So what we're really asking is... Have you never seen him in person before?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: I've lived in the desert my whole life. Guess you could say... I've never had the pleasure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Why does Paimon feel like this guy's not being straight with us...

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: C'mon, we've only just met. If I give you all the answers up front, you'll have nothing left to look forward to.

choices.text: You were the one who tricked Urraca, right?
Have you ever been to the Akademiya?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: No. Not once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: I have no need to go there — not when the taverns are full of the Urracas of this world. Besides, we're well aware of what goes on at that place.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you saying you have spies inside the city?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Spies? Heh, it's not as clandestine as that. The city gates are wide open, anyone's free to walk in. You can find out all you need to know just by walking around town and hearing the word on the street.

choices.text: You were the one who tricked Urraca, right?
That's all I wanted to ask.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Mhm.

choices.text: That's all I wanted to ask.
Have you ever been to the Akademiya?
That's all I wanted to ask.
Have you ever been to the Akademiya?
That's all I wanted to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Ah, here he is.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Grandfather, the person you wish to see is here.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Well done, Sethos.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Greetings, one and all. I am Bamoun, the current leader of the Temple of Silence. I know why you are here, and I thank you for your patience... Bring him out.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyrus, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Watch what you're doing!

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Ah, my apologies, we have no intention of causing you distress. But you must understand, Cyrus is of great importance to us. We had to find a way to bring him back to us.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Cyrus owes me his life, and to the Temple of Silence he owes a debt of gratitude. I let him go a long time ago, but now, the time has come to demand payment.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wanted to end my feud with this old bag of bones before you caught up with me... But you got here so quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Just leave, Cyno. This is a matter between us two old men. You're all too young to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So that's why you didn't want to report the letter. You'd made up your mind to come here from the beginning... You only left in such a hurry to try and throw us off your trail.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Some things in life catch up with you no matter what you do. You shouldn't have come... let alone brought the others.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Cyno didn't make us do anything. We came here for the same reason he did — to rescue you. We'd appreciate you telling us the truth, otherwise it seems a little unfair on everyone who had to stay behind.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: My secrets are secret for good reason... Bringing them to light can only lead to misfortune.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: You're afraid, aren't you? You can't bring yourself to speak of your past deeds to the students you nurtured as if they were your own children.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: You recognized our emblem because for many years, you lived among us. Indeed, you all but became one of us.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: You knew as soon as you saw the letter that we, not Urraca, were the ones speaking to you. It threatened you only because you know what you did. Your own guilt convicted you.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: For you, Cyrus, are a traitor! You once shared your learning with us, and joined us in our mission to revive the might of Hermanubis, to bring new hope, new opportunity...

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: But then, you betrayed us. You bargained for your independence with your past contributions. And then you left, taking with you Hermanubis's might and the wielder of his power.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: We both know what I said to you that day. That as the leader, I grant you permission to leave, but that one day, the sands of time will catch up with you. And when that day comes, you must pay the price you owe.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Ha, you really know how to hold a grudge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hermanubis' might... and the wielder of his power?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Does he mean you?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor? Anything to say?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Bamoun is right. I came here once before.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: He rescued me from the brink of death once, many years ago in the desert. When he learned that I was a scholar, he invited me to come here, and revive the might of Hermanubis together.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It was a... great, daring plan, and one shrouded in secrecy. The Temple of Silence had been bereft of Hermanubis for too long. The strength of its faith and its warriors were waning...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Bamoun proposed that we implant Ba Fragments, shards of Hermanubis, into the bodies of suitable vessels. If the experiment was successful, the spirit of Hermanubis would then dwell within the vessel.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Many believers volunteered themselves for the experiment, but we soon discovered that the bodies of grown adults could not withstand Hermanubis's power. In the end, Bamoun offered his own adoptive grandson.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: One other child was identified as a suitable vessel... and his parents agreed to release him into our custody, in exchange for a small fortune. These two children were our only hope for hosting Hermanubis's power.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: For many years, the Temple of Silence had been in possession of two Ba Fragments from Hermanubis. As remnants of his raw power, they were exceedingly rare treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: The test subjects were sent into a room that had been prepared for the ceremony, and instructed to approach the Ba Fragments, whose power had been amplified. If, after some time, this power did not repel them, this would mean that they were suitable vessels.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: The original plan was for a three-stage experiment: resonance, implantation, and recovery and observation. The resonance stage went quite smoothly for both candidates.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: As the second stage began, I realized a decision had to be made. Should we implant the fragments one at a time? This would allow us to monitor the results after the first round, and adjust our plan accordingly. Or alternatively, we could implant each fragment in a different vessel at the same time, and compare their effects.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: But as I was deliberating, both Ba Fragments suddenly became active. They glowed with a light we had never seen before... I knew that if they were not implanted right away, they would disintegrate, and be gone from the world for good.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Our two vessels had both displayed great promise by successfully resonating with the fragments. Under the circumstances, the thought of implanting both fragments into the same vessel seemed out of the question.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: To preserve our faith and our power... We implanted each of them with a single fragment.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ultimately, I ended the experiment and left, taking one of the children with me.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: In recognition of your past contributions, I chose not to send someone to hunt down and kill you both. Your lives were spared, but I have paid a great price for your betrayal ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: I have always wanted to see you, Cyno. Losing you and your Ba Fragment dealt us a devastating blow. We've been in decline ever since you left.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I see... So that's how I gained my power.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Look... In essence, I borrowed your Ba Fragment for a decade or so, and now you are seeking justice. If you want to take my life, then so be it. I'm an old man now, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But you cannot lift a finger against Cyno. He is the General Mahamatra. Your actions would be seen as a declaration of war against the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: I'm sure you don't remember anymore, dear Cyno, but you've met us all before. You were so young then, when we all gathered around and celebrated the revival of our lord.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: You and he, Sethos — you were our final hope.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You'd like me to return my power?

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: As a follower of Hermanubis, I have allowed this power to remain in the rainforest for far too long. Now, it is time to reclaim it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: That power is not yours to reclaim! Cyno was chosen by the gods, you cannot take what they have bestowed!

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: You are wrong. Cyno was chosen, but he was not the only one. My child, Sethos, has the same gift as he.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So those are your terms for freeing the professor?

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Despise me all you want. My sins are my own — the Temple of Silence is an innocent party. It is because of my foolishness all those years ago that the temple's glory has waned, and now I must take responsibility for the decision I made back then.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is, the power of one Ba Fragment is not enough. You're asking me to return the one in my possession, so it can be implanted in him instead?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Divine power causes great suffering to those who wield it. How do you know that Sethos would be able to withstand it?

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: He is no longer a small child. But regardless, this burden is ours to bear, and your objections mean little given that you turned your back on us long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Both my heart and my mind are telling me that what you are proposing is a terrible idea. However...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Don't listen to him, Cyno! That power is no more yours to give than it is his to take! You have to understand!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I know. But if this is a question of your freedom versus a fragment of power, then... There is nothing to debate.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt, but in my view, there are a number of contentions here that still need addressing.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Say that Cyno refuses to return his power, and you also refuse to release Cyrus. Then we are at an impasse. I find it hard to believe that you went to all this effort without planning for that possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You're trying to gauge where we stand while keeping your remaining cards close to your chest. Well, my stance is — put the rest of your cards on the table. Then we can have a discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Wait, those ears... So, we have a descendant of the Valuka Shuna in our midst? Splendid... Hahaha, fate smiles upon us after all!

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Everything we have longed for, Hermanubis will provide. Perhaps, this very day... *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: *cough*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is he coughing so much? He looks like he's in really bad shape...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Bamoun's condition is critical. He must have been forcing himself to act strong...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (His eyesight must be failing him, too. Otherwise, he would have noticed Tighnari's ears right away.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Bamoun! You...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Take our leader back to his room.

dialogues.speaker: Bamoun
dialogues.text: Sethos! *cough*... You...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Grandfather, I know what you wish to say. Leave this in my hands.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I don't like to drag out conversations, so I'll just cut to the chase.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Had Cyrus not stopped the experiment all those years ago, the plan would most likely have been a success. The wisdom of Hermanubis would have been ours.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Still, it's no use talking about what-ifs. We cannot change the past.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I'm not like my grandfather. The Temple of Silence has a grand legacy and a sacred duty to fulfill, so it's somewhat inevitable for the leader to have an inflated sense of self.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: But I see things a little differently. I don't believe the Temple has the same stature that it once did. Time has worn away at its prestige, and changed things almost beyond recognition.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: So I'm not going to force your hand. You're all free to leave — except for Cyrus. My grandfather gave him his chance once, and now I'm giving the rest of you yours.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Haha... You have courage and wise judgment, kid. Reminds me a lot of Bamoun in his younger years.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I just... I truly wish that the Temple would take an objective look at the Akademiya of today. You've been to the city yourself. I'm sure you've seen that much has changed for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: And things will only continue to improve. Why not consider cooperating with the Akademiya once more?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: If you hadn't betrayed my grandfather, I might well be open to persuasion. But it's a bit too late for that now, Cyrus.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tighnari made a good point earlier. He said there has to be more to your plan than this, and I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: All you and Bamoun are after is the Ba Fragment. The professor will accept whatever fate you deem fit for him out of a sense of guilt — I am the one who has a choice to make, and that's how it was always going to be.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ultimately, you want to trade the Ba Fragment for the professor, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I'm glad to see you're giving it some serious consideration.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I won't forsake my professor, nor do I intend to run from a problem that I must face sooner or later. Give me one night to make my decision.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: That works. Then I'll be waiting to hear your verdict, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh, my grandfather still has a fair few things he wants to say to Cyrus, so I'll be escorting him back now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Are you sure about negotiating with him?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I need to think this through. Everyone, let's meet again later tonight. Until then, take some time for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... Well, don't put too much pressure on yourself, Cyno! If you need any help working things out, just come and find us!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Cyno should count himself lucky that {NICKNAME} and Tighnari got here when they did. What was he thinking, trying to play the lone hero?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The desert tests the character of all who enter it, and only those with wisdom and courage shall prevail. But take heart. With his companions by his side, no harm will come to Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: (Whatever they're getting themselves into, I just hope it isn't too dangerous. Get home safe, everyone.)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: (Gods above, I pray that you will see the goodness in their hearts, and give them your protection.)

dialogues.speaker: Carefree Desert-Dweller
dialogues.text: (Huh. Those guys are pretty cautious. They just sent one person to try to talk to us.)

dialogues.speaker: Irritable Desert-Dweller
dialogues.text: (These are the guys we've been waiting for, huh? They ain't what I expected.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (Professor...)

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (The situation's even more complicated than I expected. I should make sure I know the way out before we go any further.)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (These guys clearly care a lot about each other. This is a long way for them all to come.)
